title: graph/v12
description: v12 (2026-10-17, F29-R3, R4; D-25 v3.44): each row carries `label`, `label_source` and `claim` (the statement's short name, where it came from, and its claim in notation from its current statement gloss, or null), and each decomposition its `approach`, the one-line attack the partial declares or, for an older partial, what was read from its leading comment or its annex, or null. v11 (2026-10-16, F08-T42; D-12 v3.43): rows no longer carry `circular`; the circularity claim and its label are retired, a hole definitionally equal to an ancestor being refused at the gate. v10 could not be edited (D-34). v9 (2026-10-12, F26-R17; D-9 v3.39): the document carries `review`, the target's formalization review state, and `open_pairs`, the pair directions the review leaves open as claimable work. v8 (2026-10-12, D-12 v3.38; built 2026-10-10 as v7 and renumbered at the merge, F25's v7 having landed first): each node's lemmas, the restated nodes under other branches it may draw on once proved; a decomposition's hole may resolve to one. v7 (2026-10-10, F25-R7; D-10 v3.37): the document carries `registrations`, the target's registrations in public registries (Palomar), as targets-index/v10 publishes them on the row. v6 could not be edited (D-34). targets/<id>/graph.json (D-25, D-35): every node of one target with its derived status, regenerated on every merge and never hand-edited. v6 (2026-10-08, F08-T39; D-12 v3.35, D-25 v3.35): each row carries `circular`, the merged circularity claims that say a proof of the node proves an ancestor — a label, where v5's cause `circular` took the node off the frontier — and `literature` / `literature_proposed`, the node's literature status as confirmed by a steward or curator and as proposed by a contributor. The cause `circular` is never emitted. targets/<id>/graph.json (D-25, D-35): every node of one target with its derived status, regenerated on every merge and never hand-edited. v5 (2026-10-04, F08-T36; D-16 v3.28, D-18 v3.28): each row carries `defect_claims`, every defect claim filed against the node with its file, class, whether it stands or has been withdrawn, and whether a curator's disputed record accepts it. v4 could not be edited (D-34). targets/<id>/graph.json (D-25, D-35): every node of one target with its derived status, regenerated on every merge and never hand-edited. v3 (2026-09-12, F12-R13; D-30 v3.12): each row carries `relevance` — for a variant labelled `related`, whether one signature on the sentence that says why it bears on the target is on record (nodes/<id>/relevance.yaml, relevance/v1), with the signer and date; a related variant is published as pertinent to the target only with it. Null for every other node. v2 could not be edited (D-34). status gains refuted and defective — what a merged counterexample and a merged vacuity certificate make of a node (D-12 #2, #3) — and each node gains cause, the machine-readable reason a derived status is what it is: dep-refuted for a node under a refuted one, witness-missing for a compiler-derived child whose witness slot is still a stub (D-29, F07-R6). v1 stays readable; a graph rendered by an older gate has neither value. v4 (2026-10-03, F08-T27; D-12 v3.25): each row carries `uses` — the nodes its merged proof's header declares beyond its deps (F08-R19) — and `proofs`: each merged proof of the node, its Proof.lean first and then its alternates (D-25 v3.13), with the attestation it was merged under and `used`, the nodes its proof term rests on as step 8 read them (attestation/v6's footprint, or for an older merge the target's .footprint-cache.json); `used` is null where nothing measured it, which is never the same as empty. `deps` stays what the node declared, read through revisions. The top level carries `target_proofs` (F18-R1, R2): each way the target is proved, with its closure by use. Each row also carries `decompositions` (F18-R4): the node's merged partials with the annex each cites and the holes each made. And `proposed_for` (F18-R8): the node a crux was proposed for. And `outline` (F18-R7): the stepped outline the node's decomposition followed, step by step. v10 (F28-T8, D-12 v3.42): each node's closure.

rendered_from.description: the graph commit the products were rendered from; null for an uncommitted tree

relation.description: D-30 label for a variant; null otherwise

trust_base.description: compiler when the proving attestation says so (F02-R9); kernel for a proof the kernel checked; null when unproved

proof_commit.description: merge commit of the proof when proved

cause.description: Why this status, where the reason is mechanical; null when it needs none; never `circular` since v6 (D-12 v3.35), and the circularity label itself retired (D-12 v3.43)

relevance.description: D-30 v3.12: for a related variant, the one human act on the one claim no kernel checks; null for any other node.

uses.description: F08-R19: the nodes the merged proof's use lines name

proofs.description: F08-T27: each merged proof of the node, Proof.lean first

decompositions.description: F18-R4: each merged partial of the node in the record's order: its file, the annex it cites (D-31) or null, and each hole by name with the node it became (a lemma's node when the hole restated a node under another branch, D-12 v3.36; null when the tree holds none).

approach.description: F29-R4 (D-12 v3.44): the route's one-line approach: the partial's `-- approach:` line; for a partial merged before v3.44, its first comment paragraph after the assembly opens (annex, licence and approach lines aside), else the first sentence of the annex it cites; null when none. Contributor text: untrusted downstream.

proposed_for.description: F18-R8 (D-14 v3.26): the node of the target this one was proposed for, from its latest proposed-for record, read through revisions; a pointer, from which nothing is derived. Null without one.

outline.description: F18-R7 (D-31 v3.26): for a node whose most recent stepped decomposition cites an annex/v2 annex with steps, that annex, the partial that followed it, and each step in the annex's order with the hole node named after it and its status (null for a step the assembly carries). A summary is contributor text, data only. Null otherwise.

defect_claims.description: Every defect claim filed against the node that validates, oldest first, withdrawn ones included (D-16 v3.28: every claim is shown). A claim blocks nothing by being filed; what blocks is a curator's disputed record accepting it (D-18 v3.28), and `accepted` says which claim that record names.

file.description: the claim file, relative to the node: defects/<file>

class.description: the claim's defect class as filed (defect-claim/v1 to v3)

state.description: withdrawn when a merged withdrawal/v1 record names the claim (D-18 v3.27), standing otherwise

accepted.description: true when the node's standing disputed record names this claim: a curator has accepted it for adjudication (D-18 v3.28)

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

record.description: the literature record this reading rests on, relative to the node

confirmed_by.description: the steward of the target or curator whose signed record confirms it (D-32 v3.35)

confirmation.description: that signed record, relative to the node; the same file as `record` when the steward or curator stated the status themselves

literature.description: D-25 v3.35: the latest literature status a steward of the target or a curator has confirmed, with its records; null when none.

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

record.description: the literature record this reading rests on, relative to the node

literature_proposed.description: D-25 v3.35: the latest literature status a contributor has proposed that no later confirmed record covers, awaiting a steward or curator; null when none.

lemmas.description: D-12 v3.36: META.yaml's lemmas in the record's order — {hole, node} — the nodes under other branches a merged partial of this node restated as holes. A hole's standing: drawn on once proved, never waited on.

closure.description: D-12 v3.42 (F28-T8): how the node is proved by closure, or null: the link the gate joined (a route of its merged decomposition, or at the root a resolves variant), its inputs, and the signed record beside the node. The node reads proved from it only while every input is proved, and a root only with its statement vouched as step 9 accepts; a record on a node that does not read proved is shown here all the same, so a reader sees what is waiting.

label.description: F29-R3 (D-3 v3.44): the statement's short name: its current statement gloss's label, else the name its hole bore in the route that made it, else the target's title (a root), else its id. Contributor text where label_source is gloss or hole: untrusted downstream.

label_source.description: Where the label came from (D-25 v3.44): `gloss` a statement gloss; `hole` the hole's name in a merged partial; `target` the target's title; `id` the node id, nothing else being on the record.

claim.description: F29-R3: the statement in notation, the opening display ($$...$$, without the delimiters) of its current statement gloss; null when the node has no statement gloss or its gloss does not open with one. Contributor text: untrusted downstream.

target_proofs.description: F18-R1, R2: every way the target is proved, the root's proofs first, then each proved resolves variant's, in the record's order; each with the nodes its term rests on. Ranks nothing (D-25).

closure.description: the proof's node and every node its term rests on, sorted

unmeasured.description: the nodes of the closure whose proof's use nothing measured; the closure follows their declared dependencies

registrations.description: F25-R7 (D-10 v3.37): the target's registrations in public registries, derived from its registration records — the latest per registry id, withdrawn ones set aside; empty for most targets.

review.description: F26-R17 (D-9 v3.39): the target's formalization review as the records derive it — `none` when no review record exists, `open` while it runs, `needs-intent-signer` when questions wait and no one can answer them, `complete` when one cluster survives with no open question. Never a verdict: the grade is what was signed.

grade_cap.description: the cap when no person-written candidate is in the surviving cluster (D-9 v3.39)

open_pairs.description: F26-R8 (D-9 v3.39): the pair directions left open, each a and b candidate ids and the direction, in the order the records give them; nothing is ranked
